course_name_original: Elasticidad y ampliación de resistencia de materiales
course_name_en: Elasticity and Advanced Strength of Materials

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of the fundamentals of elasticity
Greater mastery of strength of materials
Greater knowledge of deformations in bar elements
Ability to apply elasticity and strength of materials to the analysis of the behavior of machines, structures and resistant elements in general
Ability to make decisions about the material characteristics, shape and appropriate dimensions that an element must have to resist the actions to which it is subjected
Knowledge of different problem-solving methods and ability to select the most appropriate one in each case

syllabus_topics: Introduction to the study of elasticity
Simple bending: Shear stresses. Zhuravski's formula
Shear stresses in thin-walled open cross-section beams
Compound bending: Normal stresses. Neutral axis
Combined bending and torsion in circular section shafts
Shear center, torsion center or shear force center. Calculation of stresses and deformations in plane-spatial structures
Strain energy in: Tension-compression/shear/bending/torsion/general case. Clapeyron's theorem
Reciprocity theorem or Maxwell-Betti's theorem. Application to the calculation of deformations and hyperstatic reactions
Castigliano's theorem. Mohr's integrals. Application to the calculation of deformations and hyperstatic reactions
assessment_rules: To pass the course, a minimum score of 5 out of 10 is required. A minimum of 4 in the problem-solving tests is required to combine with the lab practice grade. Students who opt out of continuous assessment can take a final exam worth 100% of the grade. In the extraordinary session, there will be a single exam covering all content, worth 100%, with a minimum passing grade of 5/10. Unethical behavior will result in a failing grade (0.0).
